title: Brief Answers to the Big Questions
pitch: Hawking's last book answers ten big questions, from God to black holes. One whole chapter asks whether AI will outsmart us, and warns it could be the best or worst thing to happen to humanity.
toc_note: Chapter structure checked against a catalogued edition. English titles as used in the English editions.

chapters.t: Why We Must Ask the Big Questions
chapters.g: Hawking's life story and why curiosity matters.
His view that physics can explain the universe without a creator.
The Big Bang and the origin of the universe.

chapters.t: Is There Other Intelligent Life in the Universe?
chapters.g: Why we have not met aliens, and what that might mean.
Determinism, chaos and the limits of prediction.

chapters.t: What Is Inside a Black Hole?
chapters.g: Black holes, Hawking radiation and the information paradox.
Wormholes and why travel to the past may be ruled out.
Threats like climate change and nuclear war, and why we need a long term plan.
The case for spreading beyond Earth.
Hawking's AI chapter: intelligence is not limited to biology, AI could surpass us, and we must make sure its goals align with ours.

chapters.t: How Do We Shape the Future?
chapters.g: A closing call to stay curious and to shape the future wisely.

ideas: AI could be the best or worst thing ever to happen to humanity.
There is no physical law that stops machines from being smarter than us.
We need research on making AI's goals match ours.

args.a: Superintelligent AI could be humanity's biggest event, for good or bad.
args.c: Some say Hawking, a physicist, was speaking outside his field, though many AI researchers share the concern.

questions: Why do you think Hawking included AI among the ten biggest questions?
Which other chapter connects most to AI risk?

o: What Is Inside a Black Hole?
quiz.w: It is the tenth of the eleven chapters.

quiz.q: What did Hawking say AI could be?
o: The best or worst thing to happen to humanity
quiz.w: He saw both huge benefits and huge risks.
